stated: Create a new ‘Patients Charter’ to harness lived experience of patients and embed patient voice, partnership and safety standards across health and care settings, including: A new legal right to a second opinion. A new legal right to maintain contact in all health and care settings. Protecting patient data and patients’ rights to opt out of data sharing.

bearing_set.reason: Directly reforms patient access rights and safety standards within health and care settings, affecting how and when people receive treatment and how complaints/second opinions are handled.

Creates new legal rights (second opinion, contact, data opt-out) that constitute enforceable civil entitlements and privacy protections — squarely within the legal-rights and privacy indicators of O9.

The legal right to maintain contact in 'all health and care settings' explicitly covers care homes and residential care, directly improving dignity and access conditions for elderly people in social care — a core O8 indicator.
Protecting patient data and a legal right to opt out of data sharing directly addresses privacy rights and freedom from institutional coercion over personal health data — a concrete O10 bearing.

membership_note: Three distinct bearings: O3 for the healthcare-quality and patient-safety elements, O8 for the care-settings contact right which specifically protects elderly and social care residents, and O10 for the data-privacy and opt-out provisions. No material fiscal or labour-market effects are specified.
